impl DeclarationResolutionStorage for ExposedDataPipeline {
    async fn read_resolution_input(&self) -> Result<ResolutionInput, EntityIngestionError> {
        let destination = self.resolved_declarations_path();
        if fs::try_exists(&destination).await.map_err(read_error)? {
            return Err(write_error("resolved declarations already exist").into());
        }
        let directory = self.cleaned_declarations_path();
        let (observations, observation_digest) =
            read_table::<Observation>(&directory.join("funders.parquet"), &funders_schema())?;
        let (payments, payment_digest) = read_table::<Payment>(
            &directory.join("funding_entries.parquet"),
            &funding_schema(),
        )?;
        ResolutionInput::new(
            observations,
            payments,
            BTreeMap::from([
                ("funders.parquet".into(), observation_digest),
                ("funding_entries.parquet".into(), payment_digest),
            ]),
        )
    }
    fn resolution_run_key(&self) -> String {
        crate::domain::models::entity_ingestion::IngestionKey::from(self.key()).to_string()
    }
    async fn publish_resolution(
        &self,
        result: &ResolvedDeclarations,
    ) -> Result<(), EntitySearchPipelineError> {
        let destination = self.resolved_declarations_path();
        let parent = destination
            .parent()
            .expect("resolved declarations have a parent");
        fs::create_dir_all(parent).await.map_err(write_error)?;
        let staging = parent.join(format!(".declarations-{}", Uuid::now_v7()));
        let publication = async {
            if fs::try_exists(&destination).await.map_err(write_error)? {
                return Err(write_error("resolved declarations already exist"));
            }
            fs::create_dir(&staging).await.map_err(write_error)?;
            write_table(
                &staging.join("observation_resolution.parquet"),
                observation_schema(),
                &result.observations,
            )
            .await?;
            write_table(
                &staging.join("payment_attribution.parquet"),
                attribution_schema(),
                &result.attributions,
            )
            .await?;
            write_table(
                &staging.join("pair_decisions.parquet"),
                pair_schema(),
                &result.pairs,
            )
            .await?;
            fs::write(
                staging.join("manifest.json"),
                serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&result.manifest).map_err(write_error)?,
            )
            .await
            .map_err(write_error)?;
            publish_directory(&staging, &destination).map_err(write_error)
        }
        .await;
        if publication.is_err() {
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&staging).await;
        }
        publication
    }
}

#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "linux"))]
fn publish_directory(staging: &Path, destination: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    use std::{ffi::CString, os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt};
    let staging = CString::new(staging.as_os_str().as_bytes())?;
    let destination = CString::new(destination.as_os_str().as_bytes())?;
    #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
    let result =
        unsafe { libc::renamex_np(staging.as_ptr(), destination.as_ptr(), libc::RENAME_EXCL) };
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    let result = unsafe {
        libc::renameat2(
            libc::AT_FDCWD,
            staging.as_ptr(),
            libc::AT_FDCWD,
            destination.as_ptr(),
            libc::RENAME_NOREPLACE,
        )
    };
    if result == 0 {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error())
    }
}
#[cfg(not(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "linux")))]
fn publish_directory(_staging: &Path, _destination: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    Err(std::io::Error::other(
        "atomic resolution publication requires macOS or Linux",
    ))
}

fn read_table<T: DeserializeOwned>(
    path: &Path,
    expected: &Schema,
) -> Result<(Vec<T>, String), EntitySearchPipelineError> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(read_error)?;
    let digest = format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(&bytes));
    let reader =
        ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder::try_new(bytes::Bytes::from(bytes)).map_err(read_error)?;
    for required in expected.fields() {
        let actual=reader.schema().field_with_name(required.name()).map_err(|_|read_error("cleaned declarations lack the resolution schema; clean the retained raw capture into a fresh ingestion run"))?;
        if actual.data_type() != required.data_type()
            || actual.is_nullable() != required.is_nullable()
        {
            return Err(read_error(format!(
                "cleaned field {} has an incompatible type; clean retained raw into a fresh run",
                required.name()
            )));
        }
    }
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    for batch in reader.build().map_err(read_error)? {
        let mut writer = ArrayWriter::new(Vec::new());
        writer
            .write(&batch.map_err(read_error)?)
            .map_err(read_error)?;
        writer.finish().map_err(read_error)?;
        rows.extend(serde_json::from_slice::<Vec<T>>(&writer.into_inner()).map_err(read_error)?);
    }
    Ok((rows, digest))
}

/// Python subprocess adapter for the pinned Splink worker.
pub struct SplinkScorer {
    python: PathBuf,
    worker: PathBuf,
}
impl SplinkScorer {
    /// Selects the interpreter and the separately installed worker script.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns an error when the configured worker cannot be read.
    pub fn new(python: PathBuf, worker: PathBuf) -> Result<Self, EntityIngestionError> {
        if !worker.is_file() {
            return Err(EntityIngestionError::DataError(format!(
                "Splink worker missing at {}; configure resolution_worker",
                worker.display()
            )));
        }
        Ok(Self { python, worker })
    }
}

pub struct Guard {
    port: u16,
}

pub async fn search_entities(
    app: &Guard,
    params: &EntitySearchRequest,
) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<Value>> {
    let client = reqwest::Client::new();

    let port = app.port;

    let (term, strictness, entries) = (params.term(), params.strictness(), params.max_entries());
    let url = format!(
        "http://127.0.0.1:{port}/search?term={term}&&strictness={strictness}&&max_entries={entries}"
    );
    let response = client.get(url).send().await?;

    match response.status() {
        StatusCode::OK => {
            let bytes = response.bytes().await?;
            let data: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)?;
            let entities = data
                .get("entities")
                .and_then(|d| d.as_array())
                .ok_or(anyhow::anyhow!("unparsable"))?
                .to_vec();
            Ok(entities)
        }
        StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR => Err(anyhow::anyhow!("something unexpected happened")),
        StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY => Err(anyhow::anyhow!("bad url")),
        _ => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(
            "something really unexpected happened, investigate"
        )),
    }
}

pub async fn start_app() -> anyhow::Result<Guard> {
    let config = ServerConfig::from_env()?;
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await?;
    let port = listener.local_addr()?.port();
    let _handle = tokio::task::spawn(async move {
        let _ = serve_exposed(&config, listener).await;
        println!("started");
    });

    Ok(Guard { port })
}

use std::str::FromStr;
use uuid::Uuid;

use strum::{AsRefStr, EnumString};

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
/// Funder of MP declarations
pub struct Funder {
    id: FunderId,
    name: String,
    kind: FunderKind,
}

impl Funder {
    #[must_use]
    /// Creates a new instance
    pub const fn new(id: FunderId, name: String, funder_kind: FunderKind) -> Self {
        Self {
            id,
            name,
            kind: funder_kind,
        }
    }

    /// Persistent funder identity.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn id(&self) -> FunderId {
        self.id
    }

    #[must_use]
    /// Gets funder name
    pub fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }

    #[must_use]
    /// Gets legal person
    pub fn kind(&self) -> &str {
        self.kind.as_ref()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, AsRefStr, EnumString, PartialEq, Eq)]
/// All possible funder kinds
#[allow(missing_docs)] // Self explanatory
pub enum FunderKind {
    Company,
    Individual,
    Trust,
    #[strum(serialize = "Trade Union")]
    TradeUnion,
    Other,
    /// We don't know what this is supposed to be
    #[strum(serialize = "Not Specified")]
    NotSpecified,
    #[strum(serialize = "Building society")]
    BuildingSociety,
    #[strum(serialize = "Limited Liability Partnership")]
    LimitedLiabilityPartnership,
    #[strum(serialize = "Unincorporated association")]
    UnincorporatedAssociation,
    #[strum(serialize = "Friendly society")]
    FriendlySociety,
    #[strum(serialize = "Registered Party")]
    RegisteredParty,
}

/// Persistent exact-name funder identity.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FunderId(Uuid);

impl FunderId {
    /// Wraps a database identity.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn new(id: Uuid) -> Self {
        Self(id)
    }
    /// Database identity.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn value(self) -> Uuid {
        self.0
    }
}

impl FromStr for FunderId {
    type Err = uuid::Error;
    fn from_str(value: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
        value.parse().map(Self)
    }
}

use sqlx::PgPool;

/// Postgres client that wraps [`sqlx::Pool`]
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ExposedDatabase {
    pool: PgPool,
}

impl ExposedDatabase {
    /// Creates a new instance of [`ExposedDatabase`]
    ///
    /// # Panics
    /// Invalid connection string
    #[must_use]
    pub async fn new(conn_str: &str) -> Self {
        let pool = PgPool::connect(conn_str).await.unwrap();

        Self { pool }
    }

    /// Get a reference to the underlying pool
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn pool(&self) -> &PgPool {
        &self.pool
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
impl From<PgPool> for ExposedDatabase {
    fn from(value: PgPool) -> Self {
        Self { pool: value }
    }
}

            .await?;
        assert_eq!(res.len(), 2);

        let res = sqlx::query!("SELECT * FROM funders")

            .await?;

        let res = sqlx::query!("SELECT * FROM funding_entries")
            .fetch_all(&pool)
            .await?;
        assert_eq!(res.len(), 2);

    }

# Database migrations

[SQLx CLI 0.9.0](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/tree/v0.9.0/sqlx-cli) applies
the single development baseline version, with an
[`up` migration](migrations/20260915000000_initial.up.sql) and a
[`down` migration](migrations/20260915000000_initial.down.sql).
It creates the member, service, declaration, funder and funding tables, their current
constraints, and `pg_trgm` in the `exposed` schema. Application code does not
apply migrations.

For a fresh database, from the repository root:

```sh
make db-start
make db-migrate
make db-migration-status
make import-members
make import-declarations
```

The baseline uses [SQLx reversible migrations](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/blob/v0.9.0/sqlx-cli/README.md#reverting-migrations).
Each direction runs in a transaction. `make db-revert` applies the down migration,
removing all six domain tables and their data, functions, `pg_trgm`, and the
`exposed` schema. It leaves SQLx's history table in `public`; `make db-migrate`
can then apply the baseline again. The down migration uses dependency order
without `CASCADE`, so unexpected dependencies cause a transactional failure.
`make db-nuke` deletes the entire configured database and recreates it from the
baseline.

The Makefile runs SQLx from `ingest/` to load `ingest/.env`, with environment
variables taking precedence. It explicitly selects the migration directory and
the root [`sqlx.toml`](../sqlx.toml), which fixes the history table at
`public._sqlx_migrations` regardless of the connection's search path. Direct SQLx
commands from the repository root read the root `.env` instead; set
`DATABASE_URL` explicitly when targeting another database. No migration command
runs automatically during an import.

Run only one import or migration against a database at a time.

## Timestamps

Every domain table has `created_at` and `updated_at`, both
`TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`. A shared `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger function
sets `updated_at` when `OLD.* IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.*`; no-op updates and unchanged
upserts retain their timestamps. Updates preserve `created_at` unless the caller
explicitly changes it. PostgreSQL's `now()` is the transaction start time, so
changes within the same transaction share a timestamp.

All source date/time columns also use `TIMESTAMPTZ`. The importer converts
date-only values to midnight UTC at the persistence boundary, keeping calendar
dates in the domain model. It supplies timezone-aware parameters and reads stored
term starts in UTC, independent of the database session's timezone. PostgreSQL
stores instants; their displayed offset depends on the session timezone.
`members.latest_membership_from` remains text: it is a constituency or membership
description, not a date.

SQL uses uppercase keywords/types, lowercase snake_case identifiers, and
schema-qualified domain objects.

## Adopt an existing dbmate database

SQLx does not read `public.schema_migrations`. Running the baseline normally
against an existing schema would try to create tables that already exist.

1. Inspect the existing schema and compare it with a fresh database initialized
   from the baseline. Verify columns, nullability, constraints, indexes, the
   service-start and audit triggers, and the `pg_trgm` extension's schema. Old
   dbmate history alone is insufficient because the baseline has been edited during development.
2. Apply any missing schema changes in place, preserving imported data. This
   baseline includes `pg_trgm`, the later member/funding `NOT NULL` changes, and
   the timestamps described above.
   Resolve missing values explicitly before adding those constraints; do not
   replace missing source data with invented values.
3. Once the schema matches, record the baseline without executing it using
   SQLx 0.9's `migrate override skip`:

   ```sh
   (cd ingest && sqlx migrate override skip --config ../sqlx.toml --source ../db/migrations)
   make db-migrate
   make db-migration-status
   ```

4. Verify that all domain data is unchanged and the baseline is installed.
   The old `public.schema_migrations` table can remain as historical metadata;
   SQLx does not use it. Use SQLx for all subsequent migrations.

`override skip` records the current checksum without checking the domain schema.
Use it only after the comparison and any required in-place changes above.

## Editing the development baseline

Fold schema changes into the up/down pair without adding migration versions,
as required by [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).
`make db-add-migration` explains this policy and exits without creating a file.

SQLx records a SHA-384 checksum and rejects edits to an already applied migration.
It does not apply those edits to the database. For an existing database:

1. Inspect the live schema and apply the required changes in place.
2. Compare the result with a fresh database migrated from the edited baseline,
   and verify that imported records were preserved.
3. Only after verification, update the recorded checksum. From the repository

   ```sh
   ingest/.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
   import hashlib
   import os
   from pathlib import Path

   import psycopg
   from dotenv import load_dotenv

   load_dotenv('ingest/.env')
   baseline = Path('db/migrations/20260915000000_initial.up.sql')
   checksum = hashlib.sha384(baseline.read_bytes()).digest()
   with psycopg.connect(os.environ['DATABASE_URL']) as conn:
       updated = conn.execute(
           'UPDATE public._sqlx_migrations SET checksum = %s '
           'WHERE version = %s AND success = true',
           (checksum, 20260915000000),
       )
       if updated.rowcount != 1:
           raise RuntimeError('Expected one successfully applied baseline')

   make db-migration-status

disposable, `make db-nuke` installs the edited baseline instead.

# Database migrations

[SQLx CLI 0.9.0](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/tree/v0.9.0/sqlx-cli) applies
the single development baseline version, with an
[`up` migration](migrations/20260915000000_initial.up.sql) and a
[`down` migration](migrations/20260915000000_initial.down.sql).
It creates the member, service, declaration, funder and funding tables, their current
constraints, and `pg_trgm` in the `exposed` schema. Application code does not
apply migrations.

For a fresh database, from the repository root:

```sh
make db-start
make db-migrate
make db-migration-status
make import-members
make import-declarations
```

The baseline uses [SQLx reversible migrations](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/blob/v0.9.0/sqlx-cli/README.md#reverting-migrations).
Each direction runs in a transaction. `make db-revert` applies the down migration,
removing all six domain tables and their data, functions, `pg_trgm`, and the
`exposed` schema. It leaves SQLx's history table in `public`; `make db-migrate`
can then apply the baseline again. The down migration uses dependency order
without `CASCADE`, so unexpected dependencies cause a transactional failure.
`make db-nuke` deletes the entire configured database and recreates it from the
baseline.

The Makefile runs SQLx from `ingest/` to load `ingest/.env`, with environment
variables taking precedence. It explicitly selects the migration directory and
the root [`sqlx.toml`](../sqlx.toml), which fixes the history table at
`public._sqlx_migrations` regardless of the connection's search path. Direct SQLx
commands from the repository root read the root `.env` instead; set
`DATABASE_URL` explicitly when targeting another database. No migration command
runs automatically during an import.

Run only one import or migration against a database at a time.

## Timestamps

Every domain table has `created_at` and `updated_at`, both
`TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`. A shared `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger function
sets `updated_at` when `OLD.* IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.*`; no-op updates and unchanged
upserts retain their timestamps. Updates preserve `created_at` unless the caller
explicitly changes it. PostgreSQL's `now()` is the transaction start time, so
changes within the same transaction share a timestamp.

All source date/time columns also use `TIMESTAMPTZ`. The importer converts
date-only values to midnight UTC at the persistence boundary, keeping calendar
dates in the domain model. It supplies timezone-aware parameters and reads stored
term starts in UTC, independent of the database session's timezone. PostgreSQL
stores instants; their displayed offset depends on the session timezone.
`members.latest_membership_from` remains text: it is a constituency or membership
description, not a date.

SQL uses uppercase keywords/types, lowercase snake_case identifiers, and
schema-qualified domain objects.

SQLx does not read `public.schema_migrations`. Running the baseline normally
against an existing schema would try to create tables that already exist.

1. Inspect the existing schema and compare it with a fresh database initialized
   from the baseline. Verify columns, nullability, constraints, indexes, the
   service-start and audit triggers, and the `pg_trgm` extension's schema. Old
   dbmate history alone is insufficient because the baseline has been edited during development.
2. Apply any missing schema changes in place, preserving imported data. This
   baseline includes `pg_trgm`, the later member/funding `NOT NULL` changes, and
   the timestamps described above.
   Resolve missing values explicitly before adding those constraints; do not
   replace missing source data with invented values.
3. Once the schema matches, record the baseline without executing it using
   SQLx 0.9's `migrate override skip`:

   ```sh

4. Verify that all domain data is unchanged and the baseline is installed.

`override skip` records the current checksum without checking the domain schema.
Use it only after the comparison and any required in-place changes above.

as required by [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).
`make db-add-migration` explains this policy and exits without creating a file.

It does not apply those edits to the database. For an existing database:

1. Inspect the live schema and apply the required changes in place.
2. Compare the result with a fresh database migrated from the edited baseline,

item.stdout:
# Resolved declaration loader candidate design C

## Problem

The CLI currently captures declarations, cleans them, and resolves identities into a run-local Parquet output. It has no declaration `load` stage. The database schema already stores declarations, funders, and funding entries, and member loading establishes the local member UUIDs first. The loader must combine the captured declaration metadata and cleaned occurrence data with resolution and attribution outputs, then write a coherent relational projection. It must preserve every funding occurrence, including unavailable attribution, and avoid leaving partial batches. Existing storage and domain boundaries use typed domain ports, while SQL remains in outbound adapters and uses `sqlx::query!` macros.

## Usage (caller's view)

A data operator runs `exposed data declarations load <config> --ingestion-key <key>`. The command reads the selected ingestion run and writes all its resolved declarations in one database transaction. A second invocation reports that the run was already loaded and changes no rows.

The CLI adapts filesystem and database configuration, then invokes one service:

```rust
let source = ExposedDataPipeline::open_existing_declarations(&config.data_dir, key)?;
let db = ExposedDatabase::new(&data_config.connection_string).await;
let summary = DeclarationLoaderService::new(source, db).load_declarations().await?;
println!("Loaded declarations: {}", summary.declarations);
```

A service caller can use test doubles without knowing Parquet or PostgreSQL details:

```rust
let summary = DeclarationLoaderService::new(files, repository)
    .load_declarations()
    .await?;
```

The storage adapter reads captured raw partitions, cleaned funding/funder tables, and the resolution outputs, validates their references, and returns one load projection. The database adapter persists that projection atomically.

## Shape

Keep the application-facing contract to one load operation. Add `DeclarationLoaderService` in `domain/services/declaration_loading.rs`, with a filesystem source port and a database repository port in `domain/repositories/declaration_loading.rs`. Put the source adapter alongside the existing pipeline adapters in `outbound/declaration_loading.rs`; put the SQL adapter in `outbound/declaration_loading.rs` as an `ExposedDatabase` implementation, or split the SQL implementation into `outbound/declaration_loading/postgres.rs` only if the file becomes unwieldy. The CLI only selects config, constructs adapters, invokes the service, and prints its summary.

The service data shape is a checked `ResolvedDeclarationLoad` aggregate. It contains declarations, distinct identity funders, and funding occurrences. Declaration rows carry source declaration ID, stored member UUID, category fields, fetch time, and registration date. Identity funders carry the selected resolution identity key plus one display name and donor metadata where supported. Occurrence rows carry source funding-entry ID, declaration ID, optional selected identity key, amount, currency, and payment type. A missing `selected_funder_id` or an unavailable attribution becomes `funder_id: None`; it does not drop the funding occurrence. `pair_decisions.parquet` remains audit output and is not loaded into the operational schema.

```rust
pub struct ResolvedDeclarationLoad {
    declarations: Vec<DeclarationToLoad>,
    funders: Vec<FunderToLoad>,
    funding_entries: Vec<FundingEntryToLoad>,
}

pub struct DeclarationToLoad {
    source_declaration_id: DeclarationId,
    member_id: Uuid,
    category_id: NonZeroU32,
    category_name: NonEmptyString,
    fetched_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    registration_date: Option<NaiveDate>,
}

pub struct FunderToLoad {
    identity_id: ResolutionIdentityId,
    display_name: NonEmptyString,
    kind: Option<FunderKind>,
    company_number: Option<CompanyNumber>,
}

pub struct FundingEntryToLoad {
    source_funding_entry_id: FundingEntryId,
    source_declaration_id: DeclarationId,
    funder: Option<ResolutionIdentityId>,
    amount: Option<Decimal>,
    currency: Option<String>,
    payment_type: Option<String>,
}

pub trait DeclarationLoadSource: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn read_load(&self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<ResolvedDeclarationLoad, DeclarationLoadError>> + Send;
}

pub trait DeclarationLoadRepository: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn load(&self, batch: &ResolvedDeclarationLoad) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), DeclarationLoadError>> + Send;
}

pub struct DeclarationLoaderService<S, R> { source: S, repository: R }
impl<S: DeclarationLoadSource, R: DeclarationLoadRepository> DeclarationLoaderService<S, R> {
    pub async fn load_declarations(&self) -> Result<DeclarationLoadSummary, DeclarationLoadError> {
        let batch = self.source.read_load().await?;
        self.repository.load(&batch).await?;
        Ok(batch.summary())
    }
}
```

`ResolutionIdentityId` should be a private newtype parsed from the existing `identity_id` value. The filesystem adapter owns Parquet schemas, raw JSON replay, joins, and boundary checks. It joins selected observation IDs to observation resolutions, and uses the corresponding cleaned observation's `name_raw`, `donor_kind`, and `donor_company_number`. It joins cleaned funding entries with declaration metadata and payment attributions by their typed source IDs. The checked aggregate constructor enforces unique source IDs, valid member UUIDs, all declaration/member references, and that each optional funder key resolves to exactly one funder in the batch. Use existing validated `DeclarationId`, `FundingEntryId`, and `FunderKind` domain concepts where accessible; make their constructors available to this module rather than introducing unchecked duplicate primitives.

The repository owns the full database transaction. Use `sqlx::query!` statements, in dependency order: insert funders and retain an in-memory map from `ResolutionIdentityId` to database UUID; insert declarations; insert each funding occurrence using that map. Do not keep a second persistent identity map in the service. If batching is needed, use query macros in bounded chunks within the same transaction. A commit publishes the whole batch; any parse, constraint, or SQL error rolls it back.

The initial overwrite policy is fail-if-any source declaration ID in the batch already exists. Perform this check inside the transaction and also rely on unique constraints to handle concurrent loader processes. This avoids silently mixing an old set of children with a new resolved result. A repeat is a clear no-op in effect because it errors before writes. Do not use `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` for declarations or funding entries: the schema has no ingestion-run ownership key or complete child replacement mechanism. Do not claim retry idempotency beyond safe refusal. The database adapter should check all identifiers before inserts and let the unique constraints arbitrate races.

The existing baseline schema provides `declarations.source_declaration_id UNIQUE`, `funders.funder_name UNIQUE`, and funding entries referencing source declaration IDs and funder UUIDs. It needs no columns for this projection if run-local identity IDs are only in-memory grouping keys. Persisting resolution provenance or enabling safe replacement would require a deliberate schema/product decision. Keep all query SQL in the adapter and compile-time checked, per repository policy. The loader adds no new migration for the recommended first cut.

This is a deep service interface with one call hiding multi-file reconciliation and the persist sequence. Callers still provide the ingestion key through construction of the source adapter, but do not coordinate stages or handle transport/storage rows. The source adapter is the only owner of the cross-file joins, and the repository is the only owner of transaction and conflict policy.

## Synthesis decision

Independent candidate C. No other candidates were available in this isolated assignment, so there is no arena base selection or graft. The proposed shape emphasizes a checked batch boundary and one transaction-owning repository operation.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept buffering one ingestion run as a typed aggregate in exchange for validating the cross-file graph before opening a database transaction. Very large runs may require bounded SQL batches, but those remain in one transaction.
- We accept resolving identity IDs to UUIDs inside the SQL adapter in exchange for keeping storage keys out of the public domain API.
- We accept refusing a previously loaded batch in exchange for avoiding partial overwrite semantics that the current schema cannot express safely.
- We accept leaving pair decisions in the audit files in exchange for keeping the operational database schema focused on declarations and funding entries.
- We accept the schema's globally unique `funder_name` constraint as a constraint requiring an explicit naming policy. The loader cannot safely choose between aliases, duplicate same-name identities, and globally merged organizations by itself.

## Alternatives considered

- A `load` method directly on `ExposedDataPipeline` that accepts `ExposedDatabase` and performs reads, joins, and SQL would expose one easy call, but it gives the filesystem adapter database ownership and merges transport parsing with persistence. It hides complexity from the CLI at the cost of making the adapter shallow in domain terms and hard to test by port.
- Passing raw `Vec<ObservationResolution>`, `Vec<PaymentAttribution>`, and cleaned rows through a service that coordinates per-file reads and calls multiple repository methods would retain transport shapes in the domain interface. It exposes stage ordering and validation to the service and duplicates join rules across callers. The aggregate hides more complexity behind a smaller surface.
- Upserting all rows by source IDs would make reruns appear idempotent, but it would not remove stale funding entries or safely handle funder alias/identity changes. The current schema lacks ingestion-run ownership and replacement boundaries, so this alternative exposes inconsistency risk while hiding the need for reconciliation.

## Implementation reconciliation

Not implemented. During implementation, revise this section with any accepted changes to caller behavior, ownership, transaction scope, or overwrite outcome, including the source of acceptance.

## Open questions and risks

- Should funder identity be keyed globally by exact display name, by a persisted resolution identity, or by a separate verified company identifier? The current `funders.funder_name UNIQUE` forces a global name collision policy, while run-local IDs can change when component membership changes.
- Which source name should represent one resolved identity when member observations have aliases? The proposal uses a deterministic selected display name, but the product may want raw donor names, canonicalized names, or a review-approved canonical value.
- Should a later resolve run be allowed to replace loaded declarations? The proposal refuses conflicts until the database records ingestion ownership and can replace the declaration/funding-entry set atomically.
- Does loading require preserving attribution basis and unavailable reason in the database? The present tables have no columns for that provenance, so the proposal keeps it in the run's Parquet output.
- Are declaration-level funder identities without any funding occurrence intended to become rows in `funders`? The proposed funder set should include only identities referenced by payment attribution unless the product explicitly wants a broader registry.

## Next implementation step

Define the checked load aggregate and source/repository ports, then implement the filesystem adapter's three-way join against raw, cleaned, and resolved artifacts before adding SQL writes.

# Resolved declaration loader design A

## Problem

The loader must import the resolver's decisions without collapsing distinct identities that share a name. The existing database cannot do this. `db/migrations/20260915000000_initial.up.sql` makes `funders.funder_name` unique and gives funding entries no source occurrence key. `outbound/declaration_resolution.rs` publishes three result tables and a manifest, but those results omit payment amounts, display names and declaration metadata. Loading requires a checked join to the cleaned tables. Declarations without funding do not appear in `CleanedFundingEntry`; loading every declaration additionally requires retained raw capture metadata or a new declaration metadata table in the cleaning output.

## Usage

```sh
exposed data declarations load config.yaml --ingestion-key 20261008120000
```

The spelling of the ingestion key follows the existing `IngestionKey` parser. The CLI requires the key, reads `LoaderConfig`, reads `DATABASE_URL`, opens the existing resolved run, and reports committed declaration, occurrence and identity counts.

```rust
let storage = ExposedDataPipeline::open_resolved_declarations(&config.data_dir, key)?;
let summary = DeclarationLoaderService::new(storage, db).load_declarations().await?;
```

A retry with the same run and exact artifacts returns `AlreadyLoaded` with the saved counts. Changed bytes under an already loaded key return a data error. A new run replaces funding occurrences only for the declarations represented by its checked declaration metadata. Other declarations remain untouched.

## Shape

The public unit is a checked `DeclarationLoad`, which owns one run's coherent database projection. Its collections have private fields. Private deserialization records accept Parquet and manifest fields. Construction checks references once before returning the domain unit. This applies Boundary Discipline by preventing the SQL adapter from handling wire formats.

```rust
pub struct DeclarationLoad {
    run: LoadRun,
    declarations: BTreeMap<DeclarationId, LoadedDeclaration>,
    identities: BTreeMap<ResolvedIdentityId, LoadedIdentity>,
    funding: BTreeMap<FundingEntryId, LoadedFunding>,
}
pub struct LoadRun { key: IngestionKey, artifact_digest: Sha256Digest }
pub struct ResolvedIdentityId(String);
pub struct Sha256Digest([u8; 32]);
pub struct LoadedDeclaration {
    id: DeclarationId,
    member: MemberAsId,
    category_id: NonZeroU32,
    category_name: String,
    fetched_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    registration_date: Option<NaiveDate>,
}
pub struct LoadedIdentity {
    id: ResolvedIdentityId,
    display_name: String,
    kind: Option<String>,
    company_number: Option<String>,
}
pub struct LoadedFunding {
    id: FundingEntryId,
    declaration_id: DeclarationId,
    attribution: LoadedAttribution,
    amount: Option<BigDecimal>,
    currency: Option<String>,
    payment_type: Option<String>,
}
pub enum LoadedAttribution {
    Selected { observation: FunderObservationId, identity: ResolvedIdentityId,
        basis: AttributionBasis, parent: Option<DeclarationId> },
    Unavailable { reason: UnavailableReason },
}
pub enum DeclarationLoadOutcome {
    Imported(DeclarationLoadSummary),
    AlreadyLoaded(DeclarationLoadSummary),
}
```

The exact money type should reuse the application's existing decimal conversion. No floating-point conversion is permitted for money. Model the Domain changes the selected/unavailable representation to an enum rather than independent nullable fields. An unresolved selected identity is rejected unless existing resolver policy permits it, in which case represent it as a separate explicit outcome rather than inventing a funder.

```rust
pub trait DeclarationLoadStorage: Send + Sync {
    fn read_declaration_load(&self)
        -> impl Future<Output = Result<DeclarationLoad, EntityIngestionError>> + Send;
}
pub trait DeclarationLoadRepository: Send + Sync {
    fn load_declarations(&self, load: &DeclarationLoad)
        -> impl Future<Output = Result<DeclarationLoadOutcome, EntityIngestionError>> + Send;
}
pub struct DeclarationLoaderService<S, R> { storage: S, repository: R }
impl<S: DeclarationLoadStorage, R: DeclarationLoadRepository> DeclarationLoaderService<S, R> {
    pub const fn new(storage: S, repository: R) -> Self;
    pub async fn load_declarations(&self)
        -> Result<DeclarationLoadOutcome, EntityIngestionError>;
}
```

`domain/models/declaration_loading.rs` owns the checked projection and its pure constructor. `domain/repositories/declaration_loading.rs` owns the two ports. `domain/services/declaration_loading.rs` coordinates one read and one atomic repository operation, matching existing service conventions. `outbound/declaration_loading.rs` owns artifact decoding and the `ExposedDataPipeline` port implementation. `outbound/postgres/declaration_loading.rs`, or a sibling module consistent with current outbound layout, owns SQL and the transaction. `inbound/cli.rs` adds the `Load` arm. No generic import framework or configurable conflict-policy matrix is needed.

Expose the existing resolution schema and table reader only within outbound modules, or move them to a private shared Parquet module. Do not call `read_resolution_input` for loading. That method intentionally refuses when resolved output already exists.

## Validation contract

Read cleaned observations with names and company evidence, full funding rows with money and declaration metadata, all three resolved tables, and the manifest. Verify the manifest schema and supported policy version. Recompute the two cleaned-file SHA-256 values and require equality with `input_sha256`. Check manifest counts against decoded rows. Verify exact observation and payment coverage, duplicate IDs, pair ordering, pair references, score ranges and enum values. Parse UUIDs and SQL integer ranges at this boundary. Preserve `AttributionDecision` semantics and ensure each selected role refers to the same payment or the declared same-member immediate parent. Reject contradictory unavailable/selected fields in the private flattened wire records.

The current manifest has no output hashes. Compute a load fingerprint over the bytes of every consumed artifact with explicit file names and length delimiters. A database ledger then detects changing a loaded run, but cannot certify that a never-loaded resolved file was not changed. Strict graph consistency is therefore required independently of hashes.

Use raw capture metadata to include declarations with zero funding. Refactor the existing private raw reader to permit replay without its 'cleaned output already exists' publication precondition. Do not re-clean or re-resolve while loading. Verify raw declaration metadata agrees with every cleaned occurrence and observation it owns. A stronger future format would publish declarations.parquet and bind it in the resolution manifest.

Pick identity display names deterministically from usable source names ordered by observation ID. Preserve company metadata only from eligible donor evidence. Never infer company status from a payer's name. Names are labels, not keys. Preserve all identities or only attributed identities according to an explicit product decision; the minimal projection stores only attributed identities.

## Database ownership and transaction

Add nullable unique `funders.resolution_identity_id TEXT`; drop global uniqueness of `funder_name` while retaining its search index. Existing legacy rows retain NULL resolution identity and are never treated as resolver matches merely because their names agree. Add source occurrence ID and run provenance to `funding_entries`. Add a load ledger keyed by ingestion key with artifact digest and committed counts. Persist selected observation, attribution basis, unavailable reason and issues on the occurrence if the database is to support evidence inspection. The retained Parquet files remain the complete pair evidence record.

The transaction takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock shared by all declaration loaders. This serializes competing projections because the existing declarations table deliberately has one current row per source declaration. It then checks the ledger, verifies member UUID and Parliament ID mappings, and rejects updates older than an existing declaration's `fetched_at`. Equal timestamps with a different run are refused until a tie policy is chosen. Insert or resolve funders by `resolution_identity_id`, never by display name. Upsert declaration metadata, delete existing occurrence rows only for the imported declaration IDs, insert all occurrences, and insert the ledger. Commit once. SQL uses `sqlx::query!` and `query_as!` exclusively.

Make Operations Idempotent changes the transaction from unguarded append to a fingerprinted ledger operation. A crash before commit leaves no imported state. A crash after commit is a verified no-op on retry. Retrying an old loaded run after a newer run has superseded it returns its historical committed counts without reverting the current projection. Unreferenced funders remain retained; garbage collection is a separate operation.

Fold required schema changes into the baseline up/down pair. The checkout also contains `20261002203727_rm_terms`, despite the stated single-baseline policy. Inspect applied migrations and `db/README.md` before reconciling that discrepancy. Do not silently drop live imported data or update a checksum before schema verification.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept a serialized database write in exchange for a clear atomic current projection and safe concurrent retries.
- We accept loading all artifacts in memory in exchange for complete cross-table checks before any transaction starts, matching the resolver's existing memory model.
- We accept retaining full pair evidence on disk in exchange for a smaller relational change. Database-only audit requirements would change this decision.
- We accept raw metadata dependency for zero-funding declarations in exchange for importing all declarations without revising the resolver output protocol in this change.

## Alternative considered and rejected

An immutable set of run-scoped relational declaration, observation, pair and funding tables plus an active-run pointer is structurally cleaner for historical analysis. It hides replacement logic but forces every existing search/detail query to adopt run selection and changes declaration identity ownership. Reject it for this loader because the existing application reads one current declaration projection. Choose it instead if history browsing is a product requirement.

Directly deserializing `ResolvedDeclarations` and writing each row into the existing tables also loses. The result lacks source names, money and metadata, and the existing exact-name unique key would undo the resolution decisions.

## Synthesis decision

Pending coordinator comparison. This candidate favors a checked current projection with an immutable load ledger.

## Implementation reconciliation

No implementation or repository edits were made.

## Open questions and risks

Should load import every captured declaration, including declarations with no funding, or only the funding-backed subset? This design assumes all declarations.

Should a new run replace overlapping declarations, and should older or equal-time captures be rejected? This design assumes replacement with strict freshness.

Should funder search include identities that never receive an attributed payment? This design assumes only attributed identities.

Does evidence inspection need database-only access to observations and pair decisions? This design assumes retained artifacts remain available.

Should partial member captures remove declarations missing from a new run? This design assumes no deletion by absence because a run does not certify complete coverage of the database.

## Next implementation step

Build the private artifact decoder and checked projection against a real resolved fixture, proving unknown references and altered cleaned bytes fail before database access.

The existing database cannot do this. `db/migrations/20260915000000_initial.up.sql` makes `funders.funder_name` unique and gives funding entries no source occurrence key. `outbound/declaration_resolution.rs` publishes three result tables and a manifest, but those results omit payment amounts, display names and declaration metadata. Loading requires a checked join to the cleaned tables. Declarations without funding do not appear in `CleanedFundingEntry`; loading every declaration additionally requires retained raw capture metadata or a new declaration metadata table in the cleaning output.

## Usage

```sh
exposed data declarations load config.yaml --ingestion-key 20261008120000
```

The spelling of the ingestion key follows the existing `IngestionKey` parser. The CLI requires the key, reads `LoaderConfig`, reads `DATABASE_URL`, opens the existing resolved run, and reports committed declaration, occurrence and identity counts.

```rust
let storage = ExposedDataPipeline::open_resolved_declarations(&config.data_dir, key)?;
let summary = DeclarationLoaderService::new(storage, db).load_declarations().await?;
```

A retry with the same run and exact artifacts returns `AlreadyLoaded` with the saved counts. Changed bytes under an already loaded key return a data error. A new run replaces funding occurrences only for the declarations represented by its checked declaration metadata. Other declarations remain untouched.

## Shape

The public unit is a checked `DeclarationLoad`, which owns one run's coherent database projection. Its collections have private fields. Private deserialization records accept Parquet and manifest fields. Construction checks references once before returning the domain unit. This applies Boundary Discipline by preventing the SQL adapter from handling wire formats.

```rust
pub struct DeclarationLoad {
    run: LoadRun,
    declarations: BTreeMap<DeclarationId, LoadedDeclaration>,
    identities: BTreeMap<ResolvedIdentityId, LoadedIdentity>,
    funding: BTreeMap<FundingEntryId, LoadedFunding>,
}
pub struct LoadRun { key: IngestionKey, artifact_digest: Sha256Digest }
pub struct ResolvedIdentityId(String);
pub struct Sha256Digest([u8; 32]);
pub struct LoadedDeclaration {
    id: DeclarationId,
    member: MemberAsId,
    category_id: NonZeroU32,
    category_name: String,
    fetched_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    registration_date: Option<NaiveDate>,
}
pub struct LoadedIdentity {
    id: ResolvedIdentityId,
    display_name: String,
    kind: Option<String>,
    company_number: Option<String>,
}
pub struct LoadedFunding {
    id: FundingEntryId,
    declaration_id: DeclarationId,
    attribution: LoadedAttribution,
    amount: Option<BigDecimal>,
    currency: Option<String>,
    payment_type: Option<String>,
}
pub enum LoadedAttribution {
    Selected { observation: FunderObservationId, identity: ResolvedIdentityId,

Model the Domain changes the selected/unavailable representation to an enum rather than independent nullable fields.         -> impl Future<Output = Result<DeclarationLoad, EntityIngestionError>> + Send;

Expose the existing resolution schema and table reader only within outbound modules, or move them to a private shared Parquet module. Do not call `read_resolution_input` for loading. That method intentionally refuses when resolved output already exists.

## Validation contract

Read cleaned observations with names and company evidence, full funding rows with money and declaration metadata, all three resolved tables, and the manifest. Verify the manifest schema and supported policy version. Recompute the two cleaned-file SHA-256 values and require equality with `input_sha256`. Check manifest counts against decoded rows. Reject contradictory unavailable/selected fields in the private flattened wire records.

Use raw capture metadata to include declarations with zero funding. Refactor the existing private raw reader to permit replay without its 'cleaned output already exists' publication precondition. Do not re-clean or re-resolve while loading. Verify raw declaration metadata agrees with every cleaned occurrence and observation it owns. A stronger future format would publish declarations.parquet and bind it in the resolution manifest.

Pick identity display names deterministically from usable source names ordered by observation ID. Preserve company metadata only from eligible donor evidence. Never infer company status from a payer's name. Names are labels, not keys. Preserve all identities or only attributed identities according to an explicit product decision; the minimal projection stores only attributed identities.

## Database ownership and transaction

Add nullable unique `funders.resolution_identity_id TEXT`; drop global uniqueness of `funder_name` while retaining its search index. Existing legacy rows retain NULL resolution identity and are never treated as resolver matches merely because their names agree. Add source occurrence ID and run provenance to `funding_entries`. Add a load ledger keyed by ingestion key with artifact digest and committed counts. Persist selected observation, attribution basis, unavailable reason and issues on the occurrence if the database is to support evidence inspection. The retained Parquet files remain the complete pair evidence record.

The transaction takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock shared by all declaration loaders. This serializes competing projections because the existing declarations table deliberately has one current row per source declaration. It then checks the ledger, verifies member UUID and Parliament ID mappings, and rejects updates older than an existing declaration's `fetched_at`. Equal timestamps with a different run are refused until a tie policy is chosen. Insert or resolve funders by `resolution_identity_id`, never by display name. Upsert declaration metadata, delete existing occurrence rows only for the imported declaration IDs, insert all occurrences, and insert the ledger. Commit once. SQL uses `sqlx::query!` and `query_as!` exclusively.

Make Operations Idempotent changes the transaction from unguarded append to a fingerprinted ledger operation. A crash before commit leaves no imported state. A crash after commit is a verified no-op on retry. Retrying an old loaded run after a newer run has superseded it returns its historical committed counts without reverting the current projection. Unreferenced funders remain retained; garbage collection is a separate operation.

Fold required schema changes into the baseline up/down pair. The checkout also contains `20261002203727_rm_terms`, despite the stated single-baseline policy. Inspect applied migrations and `db/README.md` before reconciling that discrepancy. Do not silently drop live imported data or update a checksum before schema verification.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept a serialized database write in exchange for a clear atomic current projection and safe concurrent retries.
- We accept loading all artifacts in memory in exchange for complete cross-table checks before any transaction starts, matching the resolver's existing memory model.
- We accept retaining full pair evidence on disk in exchange for a smaller relational change. Database-only audit requirements would change this decision.
- We accept raw metadata dependency for zero-funding declarations in exchange for importing all declarations without revising the resolver output protocol in this change.

## Alternative considered and rejected

An immutable set of run-scoped relational declaration, observation, pair and funding tables plus an active-run pointer is structurally cleaner for historical analysis. It hides replacement logic but forces every existing search/detail query to adopt run selection and changes declaration identity ownership. Reject it for this loader because the existing application reads one current declaration projection. Choose it instead if history browsing is a product requirement.

Directly deserializing `ResolvedDeclarations` and writing each row into the existing tables also loses. The result lacks source names, money and metadata, and the existing exact-name unique key would undo the resolution decisions.

## Synthesis decision

Pending coordinator comparison. This candidate favors a checked current projection with an immutable load ledger.

## Implementation reconciliation

No implementation or repository edits were made.

## Open questions and risks

Should load import every captured declaration, including declarations with no funding, or only the funding-backed subset? This design assumes all declarations.

Should a new run replace overlapping declarations, and should older or equal-time captures be rejected? This design assumes replacement with strict freshness.

Should funder search include identities that never receive an attributed payment? This design assumes only attributed identities.

Build the private artifact decoder and checked projection against a real resolved fixture, proving unknown references and altered cleaned bytes fail before database access.

# Cross-judge verdict

Recommend candidate A as the base. It makes the loaded declarations available to existing consumers while correcting the schema constraint that would collapse resolved identities. Graft B's explicit separation of identity assignment from attribution and its typed manifest parsing. Do not adopt B's archival-only destination or C's unchanged name-unique schema.

These scores assess the written designs, not tested implementations. All three candidates produced complete artifacts. There were no dropouts.

| Criterion, scored 1–5 | A | B | C |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Preserves identity and attribution without collapsing distinct identities | 4 | 5 | 1 |
| Imports required metadata and every occurrence safely | 5 | 4 | 3 |
| Makes data useful to current consumers | 5 | 1 | 3 |
| Coherent transactions and retries | 5 | 5 | 3 |
| Appropriate scope and project consistency | 4 | 3 | 3 |
| Total out of 25 | 23 | 18 | 13 |

A earns its lead through its current projection, occurrence identifiers, removal of name uniqueness, and fingerprinted load ledger. It includes raw declaration metadata so declarations with no funding survive. Its transaction handles replacement, concurrent loaders, retry after commit, and retry after later supersession. Its weaknesses are optional wording around attribution persistence, an incomplete display-name fallback for company-only evidence, and a strict freshness policy that needs an explicit default. These are local corrections to a coherent design.

B is the strongest archival model. It retains all observations and decisions, separates identity from reporting selection, and scopes references to a run. Its unique run marker gives a coherent transaction and retry boundary. It leaves the key user outcome unfinished because existing database consumers would not see the imported declarations. It also leaves zero-funding metadata acquisition unresolved. Its added run tables and future serving policy make it a larger task than necessary for this request.

C has useful aggregate and repository boundaries, but the unchanged schema cannot represent distinct identities sharing a display name. Its proposed explicit naming policy is still unresolved, so the advertised projection is not implementable safely as written. It discards attribution basis and unavailable reason from the database. Its usage promises an AlreadyLoaded outcome, while the transaction section promises a conflict error. Atomic refusal is safe but differs from the claimed CLI behavior. Keeping source occurrence IDs only in memory also prevents durable occurrence-level traceability.

# Source checks that affect synthesis

`db/migrations/20260915000000_initial.up.sql` really does make `funders.funder_name` unique and lacks source occurrence IDs on funding entries. A schema change is necessary to load arbitrary resolved identities faithfully into existing tables.

`exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs` constructs two identity namespaces. Statistical and provisional identities include `run-local:{run_key}:{leader}`. Company identities use `source-reported:companies-house:{number}`. B's statement that all identity strings are local to a run is inaccurate. A's unique exact resolution identifier preserves both existing semantics without inventing a new global matching policy.

`exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/attribution.rs` selects an observation only when it has a normalized name or eligible company number. The identity implementation assigns an identity in both cases. Therefore current valid resolver output cannot select an unresolved observation. A may reject that combination as corrupt output for the supported policy. Keep selected observation and identity as distinct concepts because they mean different things, but a speculative third outcome is unnecessary for the current policy.

The same usable-company path permits selection without a usable name. A's deterministic usable-name rule needs a fallback. Prefer another usable name from the resolved component, then a stable label derived from the explicit captured company identifier. Do not reject an otherwise valid funding occurrence because its identity has no display name.

# Recommended defaults and grafts

1. Load every captured declaration. Reuse raw replay for declaration metadata and verify its agreement with cleaned evidence. Include all consumed raw bytes in the fingerprint.
2. Store only identities referenced by selected payments in the serving funders table. Keep all original resolution artifacts available for full evidence inspection.
3. Persist source occurrence ID, selected observation, attribution basis, selected parent, unavailable reason, and attribution issues with funding entries. These fields preserve the result the user asked to load. Make this part of A's required schema rather than an optional future inspection feature.
4. Adopt B's typed supported manifest contract and complete coverage checks. Preserve published outcomes and validate their references without rerunning statistical resolution or invoking Python.
5. Default to replacing only explicitly included declarations. Never delete declarations merely because a capture omits them. Reject stale captures. Reject equal-time conflicting runs with a clear error until there is evidence for an ordering policy. Exact already-loaded retries remain successful no-ops.
6. Use the exact resolver identity ID as the persistent matching key. Names remain display labels. Choose metadata deterministically from eligible donor evidence and avoid replacing richer existing company evidence with absent fields.
7. Keep one transaction and A's loader lock. Keep run fingerprint and counts in the ledger. Fold schema changes into the baseline pair and verify the live schema before any migration checksum update.

No operator question blocks implementation under these defaults. The main product assumption is that load updates the application's current searchable data. An archival-only interpretation would favor B, but it is a weaker default for this CLI request and the existing application schema.

The implementation should prove distinct same-name identities survive, zero-funding declarations load, unavailable occurrences survive, company-only selected observations load, rollback leaves no partial state, exact retry changes nothing, changed-artifact retry fails, and newer overlap replaces only its included declarations. These are proposed verification cases, not checks already run.

     3	CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm WITH SCHEMA exposed;

    14	
    15	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS exposed.members (
    16	    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
    17	    parliament_member_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (parliament_member_id > 0),
    18	    name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(name)) > 0),
    19	    party_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    20	    party_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    21	    latest_house SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (latest_house IN (1, 2)),
    22	    latest_membership_from TEXT NOT NULL,
    23	    is_current_commons BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
    24	    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    25	    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    26	    CHECK (NOT is_current_commons OR latest_house = 1)
    27	);
    28

    31	    member_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES exposed.members (id),
    32	    term_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES exposed.parliament_terms (id),
    33	    house SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (house IN (1, 2)),
    34	    source_start_date TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,

    36	    served_from TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    37	    served_until TIMESTAMPTZ,

    62

    64	END;

CREATE TABLE exposed.parliament_terms (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
    term_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    term_end TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT parliament_terms_valid_dates
        CHECK (term_end IS NULL OR term_end >= term_start)
);

CREATE TABLE exposed.members (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
    parliament_member_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (parliament_member_id > 0),
    name TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(name)) > 0),
    party_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    party_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    latest_house SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (latest_house IN (1, 2)),
    latest_membership_from TEXT NOT NULL,
    is_current_commons BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CHECK (NOT is_current_commons OR latest_house = 1)
);

CREATE TABLE exposed.member_terms (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
    member_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES exposed.members (id),
    term_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES exposed.parliament_terms (id),
    house SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (house IN (1, 2)),
    source_start_date TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    source_end_date TIMESTAMPTZ,
    served_from TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    served_until TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (member_id, term_id, house, source_start_date),
    CHECK (served_from >= source_start_date),
    CHECK (served_until IS NULL OR served_until >= served_from),
    CHECK (served_until IS NOT DISTINCT FROM source_end_date)
);

CREATE INDEX member_terms_term_idx
    ON exposed.member_terms (term_id);

---
name: technical-writing
description: "Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages."
---

# Technical writing

The goal is writing a tired engineer understands on the first read. Four layers get you there, one question each: what kind of document is this, how do sentences address the reader, how much does each sentence carry, and can any sentence be read two ways. Apply all four.

Three rules sit above the layers:

- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. "In order to" is "to". "It is important to note that" is nothing.
- **Use the short, everyday word.** "Use", not "utilize". "Help", not "facilitate". "Do", not "perform". A long word has to buy its length with precision.
- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** The rules serve the reader. A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.

The codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.

Don't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: "move", "delete", "a budget that only decreases", not "evacuate", "ratchet", or "endgame". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time. Propose a new offender and its replacement as an addition to `unslop`'s abstract-metaphor rule in your reply, with the diff. Don't edit that skill.

## Vary the rhythm

The layers decide what a document says and how much each sentence carries. A doc can obey all of them and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.

- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones that take their time carry a fact with its condition or consequence.
- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.
- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.
- Be specific over sterile. Not "schema changes can cause issues" but "a column rename fails the build".

## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)

One document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?

- Action + learning: **tutorial**.
- Action + work: **how-to**.
- Understanding + work: **reference**.
- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.

Use the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.

**Tutorial: learning by doing.** You are the teacher. The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will "learn". Every step produces a visible result, early and often. Tell them what they should see: the expected output, the prompt change, the log line. Cut explanation to one clause and a link. Teaching pauses break the lesson. Stay concrete. Write as "we", in commands: "First, do x. Now, do y."

**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence. Skip teaching. Action only: no digressions, no background, no completeness for its own sake. Link those instead. Allow forks and judgment: "If you want x, do y." Name the guide by the task: "How to calibrate the radar array", not "Radar array calibration".

**Reference: facts for lookup.** Describe. Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. Mirror the structure of the thing described, so code and docs can be navigated together. Put material where readers expect it. Generate from code where possible, so it stays true.

**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit "About..." in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.

Don't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.

## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)

- Talk to the reader as "you", in the present tense. "Will" only for things that genuinely happen later.
- Say who does what: "the compiler checks", not "is checked". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.
- Write instructions as commands: "Click Submit." State facts plainly. Never "should be done".
- Put the condition before the instruction: "To delete the document, click Delete." The reader skips what does not apply.
- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.
- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no "please" in instructions, and never "simply", "easy", or "quickly" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.
- Don't pre-announce ("we will soon support...") and don't start consecutive sentences with the same phrase.
- Link with words that say where the link goes: the page title or a short description. Never "click here". Prefer a sentence of context on the page over a link off it.
- Headings carry the point, not just the topic ("Pick the mode first", not "Modes"). Sentence case. A task heading is a bare verb phrase ("Create an instance"). A concept heading is a noun phrase. One h1 per page, no skipped levels.
- Numbered lists for sequences, bullets for everything else. Introduce a list with a complete sentence. Keep items parallel.
- Code goes in code font. UI elements go in bold. Use serial commas. Drop "etc." and say up front that a list is partial.

## Make statements load one at a time (STE rules)

- One instruction per sentence. One thought per sentence everywhere else.
- Split instructions longer than about 20 words and other sentences longer than about 25.
- Put the warning or condition before the step it guards: "If hot oil touches your skin, injuries can occur."
- Keep "the" and "a": "Remove backup file" reads two ways. "Remove the backup file" reads one.
- Give each word one meaning and one job, then keep it. If "check" means inspect, don't also use it for restrain.
- Pick one word per action and stick to it: "start", not "start" here and "initiate" there.
- Write procedures as direct commands, never as narration and never in the passive: "Install the component", not "the component must be installed".
- Avoid "-ing" words where you can. They take too many grammatical jobs and breed misreadings.

## Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)

- Keep words like "only" and "not" next to the word they change: "only fails on growth" and "fails only on growth" say different things.
- Break up long noun strings: "the proto import budget check script" becomes "the script that checks the proto-import budget".
- Make every "it", "they", and "this" point at one obvious thing. Repeat the noun when in doubt. Never use "this" or "which" to point at a whole clause.
- Don't drop verbs: "Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime" leaves Phase 2 without one. Give it one.
- Keep the small words that show structure. "Ensure that the switch is off" keeps "that" because it makes the sentence parse one way. Never trade clarity for word count.
- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: "the client and the host", not "the client and host", when they are two things.
- Say which parts "and" or "or" joins when a sentence can group two ways. "Both...and", "either...or", and "if...then" are free disambiguators.
- Use periods, not semicolons. Replace an em dash with a new sentence.
- Make text in parentheses a full grammatical unit or its own sentence. Never form plurals with "(s)".
- No slashes: write "a, b, or both" instead of "a/b" or "and/or".
- Call each thing by one name, everywhere. A doc that says "the gate", "the ratchet", and "the budget check" for one thing teaches three things. Rewording an unchanged sentence between edits costs the same way. Don't churn what didn't change.
- Skip idioms, colloquialisms, Latin abbreviations, and metaphors. A non-native reader, a translator, and an agent all parse plain constructions best.

## Voice and repo specifics

- Apply the **unslop** skill to every doc this skill touches. That skill owns the slop-pattern catalog: AI vocabulary, filler, hedging, formatting tells.
- PR descriptions and commit messages are writing too. Every layer except Diátaxis applies to them. A PR body is a briefing that a reviewer can read in under a minute. Do not paste swarm logs, SHA lists, or metric tables. Link them.
- Product UI strings are not documentation. Use your product's copy guidelines for those.
- Indent code snippets with tabs. Write real paths and real symbols. Make every count or tree claim true at the commit that lands it, and include the command that regenerates it.

## Worked example

Before:

> Configuration of the proto import ratchet budget script parameters is performed via budget.json. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. If exceeded, CI fails.

After:

> `budget.mjs` reads the committed budget from `budget.json` and counts the files that import protos. If the count exceeds the budget, CI fails. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.
